doc.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016

chapter: Black Radio and the new waves
title: Making Ah Yeah with Musiq Soulchild and Chrisette Michele
summary: Recording Ah Yeah in Atlanta; Chrisette Michele joined because her flight was cancelled; another Black Radio is planned.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Because the radio grabbed that song really quick and started playing it on the radio stations. So I started getting all these offers to do things. And thinking about “Ah Yeah,” I recorded just the music in L.A., I called up Musiq Soulchild blah-blah-blah this record blah-blah-blah-blah-blah. He’s like, “all right. Come to Atlanta, let’s record it.” So I flew to Atlanta. And I was there for three days. The first day I went in he heard it, listened to it, walked around, was kind of writing to it. Cool. He wrote a first verse. And then he wrote the second verse. He said, “I’m going to record it tomorrow.” I was like, “cool.” That night I went to a music festival in Atlanta. They had a music festival happening. Foreign Exchange was there. And Phonte asked me to sit in with them that night. He had heard I was in Atlanta. So I went to sit in with Foreign Exchange. I sat in, after I got off the keys, Chrisette Michele was there because she was ending the night. She was like, “what are you doing here?” I was like, “oh I was sitting in with Foreign Exchange but I’m actually recording an album.” She’s like, “oh word” blah-blah-blah-blah. And I was like, “how long you in town.” She was like, “well my flight got canceled, I was going to take a red eye tonight but my flight got canceled because there’s a big storm in New York.” And I was like, “what you doin’ after this?” She was like, “nothing.” And I was like, “come down the studio.” And that’s how she got on the song. Because she couldn’t get on the flight. And I saw her and I was like, “hey, you want to come down?” And that became the best part of my biggest song, radio-wise. That’s my biggest song.
So is there another “Black Radio” in the works?
Yeah. Not in the works, but definitely, I’m going to do another “Black Radio” or three, and like I said, a “Black Radio” Gospel album.
